evidence.claim: Meta says it collects information about the friends, followers, groups, accounts, Pages and communities you connect and interact with, on and off Meta Products.

Meta states it does not sell any of your information to anyone, and notes that if it sells or transfers all or part of its business, in some cases it will give the new owner your information as the law allows.
Meta lists advertisers who show ads on its Products and businesses it hires to market its Products among those it shares certain information with.
Meta says it gives advertisers reports about the number and kinds of people who see and engage with their ads.
Meta says it uses information collected across your accounts on its Products to provide measurement and analytics services.
Meta says it may take up to 90 days to delete information after starting account deletion or receiving a content deletion request.
Meta says it does not sell users' information but shares certain information with advertisers and other partners, and uses information across accounts on its Products for measurement and analytics.

Exodus Privacy static analysis of version 579.0.0.52.74 (report dated Sept. 21, 2026) found code signatures for 9 known tracker SDK(s): Facebook Ads (advertisement), Facebook Analytics (analytics), Facebook Audience (analytics), Facebook Flipper (analytics), Facebook Notifications, Facebook Places, Facebook Share, Google Analytics (analytics), Mapbox. A signature shows the SDK is present, not what data it sends.
